Carelon._comment: NCR site, one counter, seven days (the row has serve_weekends), from the client's rule sheet plus two full sample weeks. The counter already runs two bread cells, which is what 'we serve 2 indian breads' needs: one is pinned to the tawa roti staple and the other is held to a flavoured bread by the composition below.

rules._comment: '2 indian breads. One will be tawa roti staple and other will be a flavour roti or parata.' The pin takes the first cell; this holds the second to a bread that is not a plain chapatti. The sub-category list is DELIBERATELY the wide reading of 'flavour roti or parata' — 22 of NCR's 60 breads, the parathas and every flavoured chapatti, and not just the eight rows filed `flavoured_paratha`. Measured, not stylistic: the narrow five sub-categories carry only BROWN and GREEN dishes, and forcing one of those beside a brown tawa roti every day left the colour-variety rule leaning on healthy_rice, whose nine dishes could not supply enough distinct colours over Carelon's seven-day week — the plan came back INFEASIBLE blaming healthy_rice, which is the slot that ran out rather than the rule that caused it. The wide list adds orange and red and the counter solves. `poori_/_bhatura` is still out: a poori is neither a roti nor a paratha. Gated at `min_slot_count: 2` so it stands down rather than fighting the pin if the counter is ever cut to one bread.
rules.name: carelon_second_bread_is_flavoured

rules._comment: 'weekly twice panner gravy not on consecutive days'. Both halves in one rule: `exact: 2` is the count, `non_consecutive` is the gap. Week 1 of the sample runs Shahi Paneer Monday and Matar Paneer Thursday; week 2 Matar Paneer Monday and Palak Paneer Thursday — twice, never adjacent.
rules.name: carelon_paneer_gravy_2x_non_consecutive

rules._comment: '1 kofta in a week'. Selected by NAME because a kofta is a preparation rather than an ingredient — NCR's 22 koftas are malai, lauki, veg and paneer, spread across three sub-categories, and no flag marks them. Week 1's Friday is Malai Kofta and week 2's Friday is Kofta Curry.
rules.name: carelon_kofta_1x

rules._comment: 'no non veg on Tue and sat'. The counter serves seven days, so the allowed list is the other five. Both sample weeks leave the NON-VEG row blank on exactly those two days.
rules.name: carelon_no_nonveg_tue_sat

rules._comment: 'egg gravy not to be served more then onces a week'. A cap rather than a target: the client is limiting it, not asking for it, and week 1's non-veg row is chicken on all five of its days.
rules.name: carelon_egg_gravy_max_1x

rules._comment: 'white rice at 2 time max 3 time a week. No more then 2 consective days will have white rice' + 'when white rice is served we will not serve flavour rice and vice verse'. A weekday split, as Sinch NCR's is: the flavoured rice slot stands down on the white-rice days and nowhere else, so exactly one carb is served every day. MON/THU/SAT IS A CHOICE — the client fixed the counts and the no-more-than-two-in-a-row, not the days; these three are week 1 of their own sample (Steamed Rice on Monday, Thursday and Saturday) and satisfy the run limit by never being adjacent at all. Move both rules together to change it.
rules.name: carelon_flavour_rice_off_white_rice_days

rules._comment: The other half of the split: white rice (the const steamed-rice slot) on Monday, Thursday and Saturday.
rules.name: carelon_white_rice_mon_thu_sat

rules._comment: 'only different types of raita will be served.' A one-slot component with count 1 IS 'this slot must be a matching dish' (note 20). `is_raita` covers 34 of NCR's 38 curd sides; the two plain curds are what it excludes. Both sample weeks print a different raita on every one of the seven days, which the item cooldown already guarantees.
rules.name: carelon_curd_side_raita_only

constant_items._comment: The staple half of 'One will be tawa roti staple'. Indexed so the SECOND bread cell still solves — a bare `bread` pin would take the whole family and leave no cell for the flavoured bread.
